label: conj:sm-hypercharge-invariant
title: The hypercharge invariant
html:
We conjecture that the knot-state groupoid carries a hypercharge invariant: functions I_3, Y on states, constant on gauge orbits, satisfying the Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation

  Q \;=\; I_3 + \tfrac{1}{2}\,Y

against the derived charge Q of the Coulomb-charge definition, such that Y does not factor through the writhe w.

The non-factorization clause is the sharp content, and it is not an arbitrary stipulation: the proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ, so any writhe function fails on the nucleon doublet, which falsifies the writhe as a hypercharge assignment. The Lean sibling proves the factorization criterion — Y factors through w exactly when Y is constant on writhe fibres — and, as a consequence, that any hypercharge invariant forces a writhe-degenerate pair of states separated by Y. The conjecture therefore asserts precisely that the state space carries one more independent \mathrm{U}(1)'s worth of gauge-invariant data than the writhe provides.

One candidate for the second datum is recorded without endorsement in the truncation conjecture: the ribbon-framing twist, with the helon model as literature precedent [bilson-thompson2005]. Any candidate must pass two batteries before being wired anywhere: the Gell-Mann–Nishijima consistency against the derived Q and I_3 on the nucleon doublet, and the first-generation hypercharge spectrum with its \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility relations [baez-huerta2010]. A candidate that requires tuning a coupling to pass either battery is a fit, not a derivation, and does not instantiate this class.
